meta.method:
**Basis.** This dashboard keeps your June 2026 product, PK/PD, patent and market data (`data_products.py`) and adds a competitor-intelligence
layer (`data_intel.py`) from a web research refresh completed on **20 Oct 2026**, in three parallel streams:

1. **Approved & filed products** — openFDA (drugsfda API), SEC filings (LENZ, Opus, AbbVie, Viatris), company press releases, trade press.
2. **Global pipeline** — ClinicalTrials.gov, China CDE/NMPA reporting, HKEX filings, company sites.
3. **Korea** — MFDS 의약품안전나라 (nedrug), DART, ClinicalTrials.gov, and Korean trade press (데일리팜, 약사공론, 메디칼타임즈, 메디파나, 뉴스핌, 아시아경제, 한국경제).

**Threat score (1–5)** = threat to a new presbyopia-drop entrant in Korea, weighing commercial readiness, product profile, Korean channel
strength and overlap with combination/pilocarpine strategies. It is an analyst judgement, not a model output.

**Dates marked "expected" are estimates**, shown as light segments in the Korea race chart.

**Limits.** Some pages (drugs.com, Endpoints, S&P, Google Patents) could not be fetched directly; facts from them rest on search snippets and are
tagged *Reported* or *Unverified*. Cross-trial comparisons in Head-to-Head are indicative only.
openQuestions: Who licensed pilocarpine 1.2% to Jetema? (Taejoon is a circumstantial candidate only.)
Will Taejoon file CTO0307 itself? What concentration, and are the Phase 3 results positive?
Exact Kwangdong MFDS filing date (Sep vs Nov 2025) and the expected decision date.
Does Opus or Viatris hold Korean rights to RYZUMVI, and are they available?
When will Optus file QLOSI? (₩3.26B milestone is due on filing.)
Korean national-phase status of US8299079 / US8455494 and of the Somerset/Allergan pilo + brimonidine families.
Has India's PresVu actually launched? Did Tainkang get NMPA approval?
First Korean price point (비급여) once an approval lands.

summary: Five drops are now FDA-approved for presbyopia, but the US has shown how hard this category is to commercialise: AbbVie discontinued the VUITY brand, VIZZ sold only $3.4M in H1 2026, and branded prices have converged on ~$79/month cash-pay. Korea still has zero approved presbyopia drops, with three NDAs in the queue (YUVEZZI/Kwangdong, VIZZ/Lotus-Alvogen, and a newly filed Jetema pilocarpine 1.2%). The domestic threat you suspected is real: Taejoon Pharm's CTO0307 is a pilocarpine drop with a completed Korean Phase 3, formulation IP and the deepest ophthalmology channel of any player, while Daewoo and Reyon already sell 1% pilocarpine off-label. First MFDS approval is expected in early 2027.

takeaways.title: 1 · The Korean window opens in 2027
takeaways.body: No product is approved yet. YUVEZZI (Kwangdong) is the favourite for first approval, followed by VIZZ and Jetema. The first entrant will set the 비급여 price anchor and prescriber habits — timing matters more than label nuance.

takeaways.title: 2 · Pilocarpine is commoditising locally
takeaways.body: Taejoon (Ph3 done), Jetema (filed), Daewoo and Reyon (off-label 1%) all sell or develop pilocarpine. A new pilocarpine-only product needs a clear edge: tolerability, duration, PF single-use cost, or Korean data.

takeaways.title: 3 · US demand is real but slow
takeaways.body: VIZZ: ~27k packs in Q2-26 and 75% repeat prescribers, but only $1.7M net sales. Pricing converged on $79/month and $198/quarter with direct-to-patient channels. Model Korean uptake conservatively.

takeaways.title: 4 · Differentiation axes are clear
takeaways.body: Duration (VIZZ 10 h; RYZUMVI evening dose), tolerability (YUVEZZI lowest redness; RYZUMVI no brow ache), PF single-use (all modern entrants), and Korean-specific dosing (Jetema 1.2%).

takeaways.title: 5 · IP: 2030 is the pivotal year
takeaways.body: Tenpoint's core method-of-use patents (US8299079 / US8455494) expire May 2030 in the US, but a carbachol+brimonidine formulation patent runs to 2042 and Taejoon has filed on stabilised pilocarpine. Check Korean national-phase coverage.

takeaways.title: 6 · Unpartnered assets for Korea
takeaways.body: RYZUMVI (Opus keeps some Asian rights), Cloudbreak CBT-199 and the Chinese pilocarpine programmes have no known Korean partner. Arctic Vision holds dormant Korean rights to MicroLine.

korea.summary: Seven companies are positioned in Korea. Three imported products (YUVEZZI, VIZZ, QLOSI) come through licence chains; three domestic pilocarpine programmes (Taejoon, Jetema, Daewoo) and one Daewoo-made generic (Reyon) compete locally. MFDS nedrug shows no product with a presbyopia indication as of 20 Oct 2026; 약사공론 (23 Sep 2026) expects the first one in early 2027.

marketNotes.title: Price & reimbursement
marketNotes.body: No official price exists for any presbyopia drop in Korea. Pilocarpine 1% is sold 비급여 (non-reimbursed). Clinicians are cautious: only 35–40% reach ≥3-line gain, and brimonidine carries a 5–25% delayed-allergy risk (헬스조선, Mar 2026).

ipNotes.title: VUITY: generic despite listed patents
ipNotes.body: Amneal's AB-rated pilocarpine 1.25% launched Aug 2025 although Orange Book patents are listed to 2039 — the outcome of the 2022 Paragraph IV challenge is UNVERIFIED. Treat simple pilocarpine 1.25% as effectively off-patent in the US.

ipNotes.title: Tenpoint's 2030 cliff vs 2042 formulation
ipNotes.body: The broad method-of-use claims (US8299079 / US8455494) expire May 2030. US12268662 then protects specific carbachol + brimonidine formulations to 2042. A pilocarpine + brimonidine product launching after 2030 may have more freedom to operate in the US — confirm Korean national-phase status for each family.

tractionNotes.title: Only LENZ discloses sales
tractionNotes.body: AbbVie never broke out VUITY; Orasis and Tenpoint are private. QLOSI's only metric is a 49.1% refill rate (Jul 2026). No public IQVIA script data was found.

tractionNotes.title: Consensus reset
tractionNotes.body: Visible Alpha consensus (Oct 2025) had ~$45M VIZZ sales in 2026 and $1.1B peak by 2038; H1-26 actual was $3.4M. Piper Sandler cut its target to $5 (19 Oct 2026); LENZ market cap (~$113M) sits below its $220M cash.

tractionNotes.title: Price convergence
tractionNotes.body: VIZZ and YUVEZZI both sell at $79/month or $198/quarter cash-pay via direct-to-patient channels (Amazon, PHIL, BlinkRx, telehealth).

marketNotes.title: Analyst market sizes disagree
marketNotes.body: 2025–26 vendor estimates range from ~$1.6B (myopia + presbyopia drops, Coherent) to $10–20B (all presbyopia treatment). Methods are opaque — use product-level revenue (above) as the reality check.

products.approval_note: First-ever FDA-approved presbyopia eye drop. Brand discontinued by AbbVie in 2026; Amneal AB-rated generic (ANDA 217733) launched Aug 2025.
products.moa: Partial M3 muscarinic receptor agonist. Activates M3 on iris sphincter → miosis (pinhole effect). Simultaneously activates M3 on ciliary muscle → zonule relaxation → lens thickening → accommodation. Partial-agonist ceiling self-limits spasm risk compared to carbachol.
products.technology: pH-buffered low-viscosity isotonic solution; BAK-preserved multi-dose bottle
products.dosing: 1 drop each eye once daily. Second dose possible 3–6 h after first. Separate from other drops by ≥5 min.

excipients.name: Benzalkonium chloride (BAK) 0.0075%
excipients.function: Antimicrobial for multi-dose bottle. Disrupts microbial cell membranes. Lowest BAK concentration among BAK-preserved ophthalmic products; risk of chronic corneal epithelial toxicity with long-term daily use.

excipients.name: Boric acid
excipients.function: Maintains pH 3.5–5.5 preventing pilocarpine hydrolysis to inactive isopilocarpine. Mild antimicrobial.

excipients.name: Sodium citrate dihydrate
excipients.function: Chelates divalent metal ions (Ca²⁺, Fe²⁺) that catalyze oxidative degradation. Softens acidity sting on instillation.

excipients.name: Sodium chloride
excipients.function: Adjusts osmolality to ~280–320 mOsm/kg. Minimises instillation discomfort.

excipients.name: Purified water
excipients.function: Aqueous vehicle, USP grade.

excipients.name: HCl / NaOH
excipients.function: Titrates final pH to 3.5–5.5 during manufacturing.

key_trials.name: GEMINI 1 (Phase 3)
key_trials.citation: Waring GO et al. JAMA Ophthalmol. 2022;140:363–371
key_trials.result: ~26% achieved ≥3-line gain vs ~9% vehicle. Onset Day 1. Peak ~1h. Duration up to 6h.

key_trials.name: GEMINI 2 (Phase 3)
key_trials.result: Confirmed GEMINI 1 results. Both trials supported FDA approval Oct 2021.

products.efficacy_summary: ~26% ≥3-line mesopic DCNVA gain vs ~9% vehicle. Onset 15 min, peak ~1h, duration up to 6h. Distance vision preserved.
products.contraindications: Known hypersensitivity. Caution: iritis, narrow anterior chamber angle, history of retinal disease.

side_effects.note: Rapid ciliary muscle contraction (spasm). Most common discontinuation reason.
Cholinergic-mediated vasodilation.
Transient; shortly after instillation.
Miosis reduces light entry; worse in low-light settings.
Over-accommodation; temporary distance blurring.
Case reports post-approval. Higher risk in myopes. Retinal exam recommended before initiating therapy.

updates: AbbVie discontinued the brand in 2026; Amneal's AB-rated generic launched Aug 2025.

products.approval_note: Second approved; lowest-concentration pilocarpine; PF unit-dose. US launch Apr 2025. Korea: Optus licence Sep 2024 (₩24.37B), MFDS NDA not yet filed (Aug 2026). Australia: BESKA NDA filed Jul 2026.
products.drug_class: Cholinergic muscarinic M3 receptor agonist (partial, low-dose)
products.moa: Same M3 agonism as Vuity but 0.4% concentration. Sits below the ciliary spasm threshold while above the miosis efficacy threshold. Polysorbate 80 enhances corneal penetration at this low concentration. PRN use possible — designed for on-demand dosing.
products.technology: Low-dose miotic; PF unit-dose vial; polysorbate 80 penetration enhancer system
products.dosing: 1 drop each eye once daily or as needed. Single-use vial — discard after use.

excipients.name: Polysorbate 80
excipients.function: Enhances corneal penetration at low pilocarpine concentration by loosening tight junctions and improving drug partitioning into corneal lipid layers. Critical for maintaining efficacy at 0.4%.

excipients.name: Boric acid
excipients.function: Maintains acidic pH (5.0–5.5) stabilising pilocarpine against hydrolysis.

excipients.name: Mannitol
excipients.function: Provides isotonicity without chloride ions. Avoids chloride-catalysed pilocarpine oxidation. Also mild antioxidant.

excipients.name: Sodium chloride
excipients.function: Fine-tunes osmolality to physiological range.

excipients.name: HCl / NaOH
excipients.function: Titrates to pH 5.0–5.5.

excipients.name: Water for injection
excipients.function: USP WFI — highest purity for sterile PF unit-dose.

key_trials.name: NEAR-1 & NEAR-2 (Phase 3)
key_trials.citation: Holland E et al. Clin Ther. 2024;46:104–113
key_trials.design: Two multicenter, double-masked, vehicle-controlled trials. Oct 2020–Feb 2022. 35 US sites.
key_trials.result: Both trials met primary and secondary endpoints. Duration up to 8h. Lower brow ache vs 1.25% formulations.

products.efficacy_summary: Both NEAR-1 and NEAR-2 met primary endpoints. Duration up to 8h. Lower side effect burden vs Vuity due to reduced concentration.
products.contraindications: Known hypersensitivity. Caution: iritis, narrow angle, retinal disease.

side_effects.note: Reduced ciliary spasm at 0.4%.
Miosis reduces light entry.
Less than BAK-preserved products.
Less ciliary stimulation.
Retained for all miotics.

updates: Korea: Optus licence was Sep 2024 (₩24.37B) and the MFDS NDA is still not filed.
Australia: BESKA NDA filed with TGA (Jul 2026).

products.approval_note: First FDA-approved aceclidine; first once-daily drop with ≤10h efficacy; new chemical entity (NCE). Korea: LENZ → Lotus licence May 2025 (Alvogen Korea expected commercialiser); Lotus filed MFDS NDA 1 Dec 2025.
products.drug_class: Iris-selective cholinergic muscarinic M3 agonist (pupil-selective miotic)
products.moa: Aceclidine binds M3 receptors with preferential selectivity for iris sphincter over ciliary muscle. Stronger/longer pupil constriction (sub-2mm) than pilocarpine with markedly less ciliary stimulation. Hypromellose extends ocular surface residence time → 10h duration. No myopic shift, minimal brow ache.
products.technology: Iris-selective NCE; viscous solution with hypromellose for extended contact time; refrigerated PF unit-dose
products.dosing: 1 drop each eye once daily. Effect within 30 min. Discard single-use vial after use.

excipients.name: Polysorbate 80
excipients.function: Solubilises aceclidine HCl, enhances corneal penetration. Wetting agent improving drug-ocular surface contact.

excipients.name: Mannitol
excipients.function: Primary tonicity agent (~280–320 mOsm/kg). Lower metal ion-catalysed degradation risk vs NaCl. Mild antioxidant.

excipients.name: Hypromellose (HPMC)
excipients.function: KEY efficacy excipient. Increases viscosity (~15–25 cP), slows nasolacrimal drainage → extended ocular surface residence time → major contributor to 10h duration advantage. Also lubricates.

excipients.name: Edetate disodium (EDTA·2Na)
excipients.function: Sequesters divalent metals (Ca²⁺, Fe²⁺) preventing oxidative degradation. Chelates Ca²⁺ from tight junctions → increased corneal permeability.

excipients.name: Sodium citrate dihydrate
excipients.function: Citrate buffer maintains pH 4.5–5.5. Better tolerated than phosphate at equivalent molarity.

excipients.name: HCl / NaOH
excipients.function: Titrates to 4.5–5.5. Aceclidine (pKa ~9.5) most stable at acidic pH.

excipients.name: Water for injection
excipients.function: USP WFI for sterile PF unit-dose.

key_trials.name: CLARITY 1 (Phase 3)
key_trials.design: RCT, double-masked, vehicle-controlled, once daily, multicenter
key_trials.result: Met all primary & secondary endpoints (p<0.0001). 71% gained ≥3 lines at 30 min and 3h. 40% maintained at 10h.

key_trials.name: CLARITY 2 (Phase 3)
key_trials.result: All endpoints met. 70–75% pooled ≥3-line vs ~10–15% vehicle. No serious treatment-related AEs in 30,000+ treatment days.

key_trials.name: CLARITY 3 (6-month safety)
key_trials.result: Well-tolerated at 6 months. No tachyphylaxis. Sustained efficacy confirmed.

products.efficacy_summary: 70–75% ≥3-line DCNVA gain vs ~10–15% vehicle. Onset 30 min. Duration up to 10h — longest approved. No myopic shift. No serious AEs in 30,000+ treatment days.
products.contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to aceclidine or excipients. Caution: iritis, narrow anterior chamber angle.

side_effects.note: Transient, mild, self-resolving. Related to acidic pH.
Miosis reduces light entry; expected class effect.
Significantly lower than pilocarpine; minimal ciliary stimulation.
Minimal hyperemia.
Iris-selective mechanism avoids significant ciliary stimulation.

updates: Korea NDA was filed by Lotus on 2025-12-01; Alvogen Korea is the expected commercialiser.
China rights moved from Corxel to Everest (Jun 2026); NMPA approval guided Q1 2027. EMA MAA validated Mar 2026.

products.approval_note: First FDA-approved dual-agent FDC for presbyopia. Korea: Kwangdong licence (DART contract 8 Dec 2023), MFDS NDA filed Sep–Nov 2025 — first presbyopia NDA in Korea.
products.drug_class: FDC: Full muscarinic+nicotinic agonist (carbachol) + presynaptic α2-adrenergic agonist (brimonidine)
products.moa:
CARBACHOL (full M3+nicotinic agonist): Directly contracts iris sphincter → strong miosis. Contracts ciliary muscle → accommodation. Full agonism gives stronger, longer miosis than pilocarpine.

BRIMONIDINE (presynaptic α2 agonist): Blocks α2 receptors at iris dilator nerve terminals → inhibits NE release → dilator silenced. Also (1) relaxes tonic ciliary tension → reduces carbachol brow ache, (2) vasoconstricts conjunctiva → reduces redness (2.8% vs 10.7% carbachol alone), (3) increases cholinergic bioavailability in aqueous ~50%.

Net: stronger sustained miosis than either drug alone, lower side effects than carbachol monotherapy.
products.technology: Dual-pathway FDC; parasympathetic (M3) + sympathetic (α2) simultaneous targeting; PF unit-dose
products.dosing: 1 drop each eye once daily. Single-use vial — discard after opening.

excipients.name: Sodium chloride
excipients.function: Adjusts osmolality (~280–320 mOsm/kg). Both APIs are stable in isotonic NaCl solution.

excipients.name: Sodium phosphate monobasic
excipients.function: Maintains pH 6.5–7.5 where both carbachol and brimonidine tartrate are chemically stable. Phosphate buffer well-tolerated ophthalmically.

excipients.name: HCl / NaOH
excipients.function: Fine-tunes pH. Carbachol stable at pH 5–8; brimonidine at pH 6–8. pH chosen to satisfy both APIs.

excipients.name: Water for injection
excipients.function: USP WFI for sterile PF unit-dose.

key_trials.name: BRIO-I (Phase 3 — combination superiority)
key_trials.design: 3-arm RCT: YUVEZZI vs carbachol alone vs brimonidine alone
key_trials.primary_endpoint: Combination superiority over each active monotherapy (FDA FDC requirement)
key_trials.result: YUVEZZI superior to both individual active components. Met FDA combination superiority requirement.

key_trials.name: BRIO-II (Phase 3 — 12-month safety)
key_trials.design: Vehicle-controlled, 12-month — longest presbyopia safety study to date
key_trials.result: All near vision endpoints met sustained over 8h. Hyperemia 2.8% vs 10.7% carbachol alone. No serious AEs in 72,000+ treatment days.

products.efficacy_summary: Superior to both monotherapies. ≥3-line BUNVA over 8h sustained. Lowest hyperemia (2.8%). 72,000+ treatment-day safety dataset — most extensive in category.
products.contraindications: Known hypersensitivity. CONTRAINDICATED in young children. Caution: antihypertensives, MAO inhibitors, iritis.

side_effects.note: Brimonidine vasoconstriction offsets carbachol hyperemia.
Brimonidine dampens carbachol ciliary spasm.
Expected.
Brimonidine's ciliary relaxation partially offsets carbachol-driven shift.
α2 effect on salivary glands; low risk at 0.1%.
Monitor in elderly or antihypertensive users.
Brimonidine crosses immature blood-brain barrier → CNS depression.

updates: Correct NDA is 220142 (sponsor of record: Visus).
Kwangdong's MFDS NDA date is reported as Sep 2025 (Korean press) and ~Nov 2025 (Tenpoint).

products.approval_status: FDA Approved (mydriasis reversal) | Presbyopia: approved Oct 2026
products.approval_note: Approved for mydriasis reversal (NDA 217064). Presbyopia sNDA accepted Feb 25, 2026 and APPROVED (announced Oct 16, 2026, one day before PDUFA). Same formulation; indication expansion. Viatris exploring a US commercial partner.
products.moa:
PRIMARY — α1 postsynaptic blockade at iris dilator: Blocks α1 receptors on iris dilator → dilator cannot contract → sphincter acts unopposed → passive pupil constriction. NO direct sphincter activation. NO ciliary muscle involvement.

SECONDARY — α2 blockade at sphincter: Blocks inhibitory α2 on sphincter → releases brake → adds indirect sphincter activation.

CONSEQUENCE: No brow ache (no ciliary spasm), no myopic shift (no ciliary contraction), no retinal traction risk. Effect lasts up to 20h from a single EVENING dose.
products.technology: α1/α2 antagonist; ultra-minimalist PF formulation with nitrogen overlay to prevent oxidation; evening dosing; refrigerated
products.dosing: 1 drop each eye once daily IN THE EVENING. 20h duration covers following morning/day. Nasolacrimal duct occlusion recommended.
products.dosage_form: 0.31 mL PF unit-dose vials (5 per foil pouch, 6 pouches per carton)
products.storage: Refrigerated 2–8°C. After opening pouch: up to 25°C for 14 days. Do not freeze.

excipients.name: Mannitol
excipients.function: Primary tonicity agent. CRITICAL: used instead of NaCl because chloride ions catalyse phentolamine oxidation. Mannitol also acts as mild hydroxyl radical scavenger — secondary antioxidant function preserving potency.

excipients.name: Sodium acetate trihydrate
excipients.function: Acetate buffer maintains pH 4.5–5.5 where phentolamine is most chemically stable. Low-molarity acetate (5–25 mM) minimises instillation sting while providing adequate pH control.

excipients.name: HCl / NaOH
excipients.function: Titrates to 4.5–5.5 satisfying acetate buffer range and phentolamine stability simultaneously.

excipients.name: Water for injection
excipients.function: Metal-ion free USP WFI — critical given phentolamine's metal-catalysed oxidation sensitivity.

excipients.name: Nitrogen gas (headspace)
excipients.function: UNIQUE FEATURE — vial headspace filled with nitrogen before sealing. Eliminates dissolved oxygen preventing phentolamine air oxidation. Only approved ophthalmic drug with this feature. Explains why unit-dose format is required: once opened, nitrogen atmosphere is lost.

key_trials.name: VEGA-3 (Phase 3 presbyopia — primary pivotal)
key_trials.design: RCT, double-masked, placebo-controlled, once-daily EVENING dose, 6-week + 48-week safety follow-up
key_trials.primary_endpoint: ≥3-line DCNVA + <5-letter BCDVA loss at 12h post-dose, Day 8
key_trials.result: MET: 27.2% vs 11.5% placebo (p<0.0001). Secondary: 20.6% vs 6.1% at 1h Day 1 (p=0.0002). Patient-reported outcomes significant at Days 3, 8, Week 6. No serious treatment-related AEs. No tachyphylaxis at 6 weeks.

key_trials.name: VEGA-2 (Phase 3 presbyopia — second pivotal)
key_trials.design: Phase 3 with phentolamine ± adjunctive pilocarpine arm
key_trials.result: Met primary endpoint. Phentolamine alone and with low-dose pilocarpine both significantly improved near VA.

key_trials.name: MIRA-2 + MIRA-3 (Phase 3 — mydriasis reversal, approved)
key_trials.design: Two pivotal RCTs for mydriasis reversal
key_trials.primary_endpoint: Return to baseline pupil at 60 and 90 min
key_trials.result: Both met. Supported NDA 217064 approval Sep 2023. Established safety infrastructure for sNDA.

products.efficacy_summary: VEGA-3: 27.2% ≥3-line DCNVA at 12h Day 8 vs 11.5% placebo (p<0.0001). Evening dose provides up to 20h near vision — effect present on waking. No brow ache. No myopic shift. Presbyopia indication approved Oct 2026 (label AEs: conjunctival redness 21%, instillation irritation 16%).
products.contraindications: Known hypersensitivity. Active uveitis/iritis. Caution: antihypertensives, cardiac conditions, MAO inhibitors. Presbyopia indication approved Oct 2026 — dose once daily at bedtime.

side_effects.note: α-blockade lowers BP; caution with antihypertensives. Nasolacrimal occlusion recommended.
Miosis reduces light; minimised by evening dosing (patient asleep during peak).
Risk of synechiae in inflamed eyes.
Compensatory HR increase from α-blockade.
Only presbyopia drug requiring cold-chain storage.

updates: The presbyopia sNDA was approved one day before the 17 Oct 2026 PDUFA date.
Label: once daily at bedtime; most common AEs conjunctival redness 21%, instillation irritation 16%. Viatris is seeking a US partner.

pkpd.result: NOAEL = 1.0% pilocarpine BID. Slow iris responses observed at NOAEL — non-adverse and reversible. No histopathological findings at any dose.

pkpd.model: Dutch-belted rabbit · Single bilateral dose · Fixed vs unfixed combo
pkpd.endpoint: Ocular PK: Cmax, Tmax, AUC in aqueous humor and iris/ciliary body
pkpd.result: Comparable ocular PK between fixed-combination and unfixed sequential dosing. Supports safety of 1.5% pilocarpine without hypromellose.

pkpd.model: NZW rabbit tolerability + PK arms · Single topical dose
pkpd.endpoint: Pilocarpine detectability: aqueous humor, iris, lens; Draize scoring
pkpd.result: Pilocarpine detectable in ocular tissues up to 8h post-dose. No corneal, iridial, or conjunctival adverse effects. Tmax ~0.5h in aqueous humor.

pkpd.model: Young adult rhesus monkey · Topical 0.5% pilocarpine ± oxymetazoline
pkpd.endpoint: Pupil diameter; accommodative amplitude (refractometry); time to peak accommodative response
pkpd.result: 0.5% pilocarpine caused measurable decrease in pupil size and increase in accommodative amplitude. Co-admin with oxymetazoline delayed time to peak accommodative response.

pkpd.model: Human n=22 presbyopes · 1 drop/eye QD × 30 days
pkpd.endpoint: Plasma Cmax, AUC₀₋τ,ss, Tmax, t½ at steady state
pkpd.result: Cmax,ss = 1.95 ng/mL; AUC₀₋τ,ss = 4.14 ng·hr/mL; median Tmax = 0.3h; t½ ~3–4h. Systemic exposure very low — not expected to contribute to efficacy or toxicity.

pkpd.model: Albino rabbit + Dutch-belted (pigmented) · Single 35µL drop 0.5% ¹⁴C-brimonidine
pkpd.endpoint: Aqueous humor Cmax, Tmax; iris-ciliary body concentration over time; melanin binding
pkpd.result: Aqueous Cmax: 2.16 µg/mL (albino) vs 1.52 µg/mL (pigmented) at Tmax 0.67h. Aqueous t½ ~1h (albino). Pigmented iris-ciliary body: peak 20.1 µg-eq/g at 1.5h; terminal t½ = 160h (melanin depot effect).

pkpd.model: Monkey, rabbit, rat · Single + multiple doses · 0.2% and 0.5% topical
pkpd.endpoint: Drug concentration in cornea, aqueous humor, iris-ciliary body, vitreous, retina/choroid, optic nerve; radioactivity by tissue type
pkpd.result: Higher and more prolonged drug levels in pigmented vs non-pigmented tissues across all species. Multiple dosing led to drug accumulation in pigmented tissues. Posterior segment levels adequate to activate α2 receptors without retinal vasoconstriction.

pkpd.model: In vitro receptor binding assays (multiple species tissues)
pkpd.endpoint: α2 vs α1 binding selectivity ratio; comparison vs clonidine and apraclonidine
pkpd.result: Brimonidine is 1,000× more selective for α2 vs α1. 7–12× more α2-selective than clonidine. 23–32× more selective than apraclonidine. Not mydriatic (unlike apraclonidine).

pkpd.endpoint: Plasma Cmax, AUC₀₋∞, Tmax after single topical dose
pkpd.result: Cmax = 73 ± 19 pg/mL; AUC₀₋∞ = 375 ± 89 pg·hr/mL; Tmax = 1.7 ± 0.7h. ~27× lower systemic exposure than pilocarpine on a mass basis.

pkpd.model: Dutch-belted rabbit · n=4/group · Single unilateral 35µL: Brimochol vs carbachol 2.75% alone vs PBS
pkpd.endpoint: Pupil diameter by digital pupillometer under 4 lighting conditions (scotopic, low mesopic, high mesopic, photopic); carbachol concentration in iris/ciliary body
pkpd.result: Brimochol sustained pupil reduction for 12h vs shorter duration with carbachol alone. Greater pupil reduction at all 4 lighting levels. Brimonidine increased carbachol concentration in iris/ciliary body (~50% higher AUC) — mechanistically explains enhanced and prolonged PD effect. Ocular tolerance profile also improved vs carbachol alone.

pipelineSummary: Beyond the five FDA approvals, activity has shifted to ex-US filings (VIZZ in 9 territories, YUVEZZI via Zhaoke and VISUfarma) and to China, where no presbyopia drop is yet approved and four pilocarpine programmes plus aceclidine are racing. Lens-softening has failed twice (Novartis UNR844, Santen UDCA). Genuinely new clinical-stage mechanisms are scarce: Cloudbreak's CBT-199 is the main novel-vehicle miotic.
